# The Apprentice

Ranta Aalto — called Aalto (D-0108, D-0132). The viewpoint of the story and its
future. Her private childhood name remains open as prose (D-0070).

## Viewpoint and entry

> status: ratified (D-0054, D-0062, D-0219)

The story begins with the apprentice, and she remains the viewpoint character —
whether literally or as the rule of thumb for what information reaches the listener.
She is the Gen-Z/alpha proxy of the piece: a child of the collapse who never knew
the before. The protagonist meets her before the anchor enters the story, and a real
plot reason forces the adoption (D-0061) — no stray-puppy pickup.

## Identity

> status: ratified (D-0066, D-0219)

Aalto is a pre-adolescent girl at the start. Narration and every character use
she/her for her. The world is bad to men and worse to women, especially poor ones,
but gender is never her chief concern — the driving plot is. Possible later plots
about gender confusion are not part of the present characterization and do not alter
the current identity or pronoun rule.

### Pronoun protocol

> status: ratified (D-0219)

The narrator, core party, strangers, and casual acquaintances all refer to Aalto as
she/her. The former inconsistent in-world protocol is superseded: he/him or they/them
for Aalto is now a continuity error, not camouflage or characterization.

## Backstory

> status: provisional (D-0070, D-0072)

The working version ([[apprentices-orphaning]]): her community was erased not by a
monster but by administration — struck from the rolls, wards withdrawn, storm let in.
She survived alone, by an improvised scrap of the old craft, and the mind of her
parent/caregiver ended up inside the woman who would later find her. Her trauma
inclines her exactly opposite the shōnen mold: not rage — vigilance. She watches
exits, counts rations, tests floorboards, and hungers above all for the rules of
things, so she can never be caught helpless again.

## Bildungsroman

> status: ratified (D-0021, D-0075, D-0077)

Three braided strands of growing up: education as liberation (learning to truly
reason — the thing the empire fears most); the widening economic lens (each region's
survival arithmetic misunderstood, then painfully learned — the audience learns the
world through her mistakes); and the long road into adolescence — first witnessing
the world's traffic in children and the transactional adult world, later feeling
desire arrive and scramble her careful defenses.

## Voice

> status: provisional (D-0083, D-0163)

Portis's Mattie Ross as the model: formal, stubborn, exact about accounts, relentless
with practical questions, never a victim and never hot-headed. The tedious aggressive
anime adolescent is explicitly banned (D-0066).

Aalto is the audience's ears (D-0163): never too weird to us — provincial,
inexperienced, young. When Enfys goes oblique, Aalto asks the plain question the
listener would; the two never both run indirect in one exchange.

## Origin

> status: provisional (D-0080, D-0081)

From the salt fringes ([[regions]]): a coastal culture of knots, flex, and quick
reading of weather — where nothing rigid survives. It seeds her skills (knot-craft,
storm-sense, barter) and rhymes with who she is.

## Craft affinity

> status: ratified (D-0121)

Her almost-lost craft is knot-craft and cord-lore (D-0121): native micro-knot skill as the
entry to magic — knots as physical premise-holders (extended cognition), storm-wards, the
hound's treaty-collar, and eventually knotted proofs, a decentralized, illiterate literacy she
reads the way others read script (the exact inverse of the protagonist's chalk-literate
cartomancy). Weather-sense is the perceptual complement — the human half of the co-processor
pairing with the hound ([[animals]]). Two threads stay open only as prose, no longer as formal
questions: her private childhood name (Q-0002) and how the parent-ghost revelation plays (D-0070).
